note: London pub gardens and beer gardens, counted by how many independent sources name each pub. Collected 16 November 2026 and published in winter, so the article says which gardens are covered or heated now and which are summer-only. 'Beer garden' is the term most source titles use (Time Out, DesignMyNight, CN Traveller, The Infatuation, SquareMeal), so the article is titled for it; 'pub garden' is the same thing. Replaces a September draft config that recorded no collection.

scopeDecision.question: What counts as a beer garden?
scopeDecision.call: A pub's or bar's own outdoor drinking space at ground level: a back garden, a yard, a riverside terrace or a front terrace. Rooftops are excluded, following Time Out, which sends rooftop drinkers to its separate rooftop-bars guide; they are in data/topics/rooftop-bars.json.
rules: Brewery taprooms and beer halls with a garden (Big Penny Social, CRATE) count when the source names them for the garden.
Riverside pubs count when a source names them as a beer garden; best-riverside-pubs is not a separate article yet.

awardBodiesChecked: CAMRA: no garden category at national level; no branch-level garden award found.
Great British Pub Awards has a Best Pub Garden category but is national, and no London winner was found in a dated winners list (trap 12). Not counted.
The Faltering Fullback calls its garden 'award-winning' on its own site without naming the award; not counted.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: Numbered 1-24, Leonie Cooper, updated 10 Sep 2026. Number one The Faltering Fullback, two The Duke of Edinburgh, three The Flask, Highgate.

editorialLists.name: Conde Nast Traveller
editorialLists.note: Numbered 1-21 as a gallery, with no claim to be an order; recorded unranked.

independentBlogs.name: Secret London
independentBlogs.note: Has a dedicated beer-gardens guide (secretldn.com/brilliant-london-beer-gardens/, updated July 2025); the September draft's note that it had none was wrong - its on-site search did not surface it.

facetAxis.note: The September draft proposed setting (riverside / courtyard / destination). Kept as the article's grouping inside sections, but the axis that decides a visit in November is shelter, so the article leads with it.

values.label: Covered or heated
values.describeAs: a roof, retractable cover, huts or heaters over at least part of the garden

values.label: Open garden
values.describeAs: open year-round but uncovered: blankets at best

values.label: Summer only
values.describeAs: the garden or its bar closes for the cold months

knownGaps: Tier E is empty: Reddit refuses this environment (403, login redirects). No forum substitute found.
No London-specific judged pub-garden award exists to anchor tier A.
Glamour UK's 41 beer gardens was declined: its slide headings are empty in the served HTML.
The Army and Navy (named in sources, Dalston) has no operator website that could be found; not confirmed trading, so no entry. Ask Rob.
Bank of Friendship and The Chesham Arms run undated single-page sites; both list current hours with no closure notice, and both are printed with their own stated hours and no-booking rules.

The Leather Bottle's homepage says the garden is 'soon to be heated and covered' and The Castle, Tooting's garden page both says it is covered and heated and, in a banner, 'soon to be'. The article describes the huts and says no more about heating for those two.
The Scolt Head's OpenTable link timed out to curl; the article links the pub's own site.
openVenueQuestions: The Spaniards Inn is recorded once though sources spell it Spaniards Inn and Spaniard's Inn.
Hope and Anchor, Brixton is kept apart from any other Hope and Anchor; sources place it on Acre Lane.
The Albion, The Crabtree, The Prince and others are disambiguated by area because several London pubs share each name.
